text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- TREASURY HOLDS ON TO FUNDS TO SWELL ACCOUNTS
Brazil's treasury is holding back funds destined for a workers help fund and a fund for developing and improving tax collection in order to improve its balance sheet artificially.
-- BANERJ STARTS PRIVATIZATION PROCESS
The shareholders of Rio de Janeiro's state bank Banerj have approved a 200 million reais increase in capital of the bank's brokerage arm which is to be transformed into a bank and sold off.
-- FACTORING COULD GENERATE 11 BLN REIAS THIS YEAR

Brazil's factoring firms are on track to close the year with 10-11 billion reais, a 25 percent increase in turnover on last year's 8.8 billion reais, according to the National Factoring Association (Anfac).
O GLOBO
-- RIO SEES SECOND CONSECUTIVE MONTH OF DEFLATION

Prices are falling in Rio de Janeiro for the second month running, according to figures by the independent research institute Fundacao Getulio Vargas which show a 0.37 percent decrease in prices in September, the biggest fall since June 1957.
-- ELECTION OFFICIAL WANTS SIX-YEAR TERM FOR CARDOSO
The president of Brazil's Supreme Electoral Tribunal has proposed extending President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's term to six years as an alternative to re-election.
-- DOCTOR ORDERS CORPSE TO BE LEFT IN THE STREET
A doctor in Rio de Janeiro is said to have ordered the corpse of a patient to be left in the street because she was in a hurry to finish her shift and close the clinic.
O ESTADO DE SAO PAULO
-- PRICES FALL IN 14 STATE CAPITALS
Sao Paulo and 13 other state capitals recorded a fall in basic foods prices in September, according to official figures.
-- GOV'T WANTS TO INCLUDE MAYORS AND GOVERNORS IN REELECTION

The government wants to include the current state governors and the newly elected mayors in the constitutional amendment on re-election which would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term if approved by Congress.
-- SAO PAULO USES LESS MONEY IN FIGHT AGAINST AIDS

Sao Paulo has received 2 million reais from the federal government this year to combat AIDS, but the city has used only 13 percent of that money to fight the illness even though one third of Brazil's 88,000 registered AIDS cases are in Sao Paulo.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
